SUFFERING FAVORS INDIFFERENCE · ALEX MALPASS
"s is therefore evidence that favors indifference over theism"

Here s denotes the stipulated fact of suffering, and Malpass presents the comparative likelihood conclusion without claiming that theism is disproven or that indifference has the higher overall posterior probability.

"

THEISTIC BACKGROUND WEAKENS THE INFERENCE · RANDAL RAUSER
"our first person awareness of our own interior states is not infallible"

Rauser grants that trauma survivors may rationalize, yet provisionally defers to their interpretations absent overriding reasons, while still treating suffering itself as bad and acknowledging that both observer and sufferer can be mistaken.
